rationale: Adds a bounded control to the StopSign double-count finding: node 4 never accepted the StopSign and is synced by the same leader, so after re-decision its accepted must equal 5, decided 5 and is_reconfigured true, while node 5 (which already held the StopSign) is left at accepted 6 and is_reconfigured false. The run re-tests the double count and measures the control in one execution.

experiment.revision_reason: Emits one additional control event for node 4, which never accepted the StopSign, after the same sync and re-decision, and adds a comparison requiring its is_reconfigured to be true. The node 5 samples and the comparison on accepted 5 are unchanged.

scope.description: Same five-node StopSign scenario, plus a control sample of node 4 (never accepted the StopSign) after re-decision.
assumptions: The AcceptStopSign for node 4 and the Decide messages to 2,3,4 are lost, so node 4 lacks the StopSign while node 5 has it.
Held Accepted replies keep node 2 from re-deciding before node 5 reconnects.
No ticks are called; leadership is obtained with try_become_leader.
excluded: Snapshots, flexible quorums, batching, starting the new cluster and repeated reconnects.

experiment.prefix: Identical to the previous StopSign run: decide Value(1..=4), reconfigure to configuration_id 2, deliver the AcceptStopSign to 2,3,5 and purge it for 4, deliver the Accepteds to node 1, deliver the Decide only to node 5, emit ready. Cut node 1, elect node 2, discard the Prepare for node 5, settle promises from 3 and 4 into Accept, deliver AcceptSyncs to 3 and 4, hold their Accepted replies, call node5.reconnected(2) and deliver PrepareReq/Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync, emit after_sync, deliver the held Accepted replies, settle, emit after_redecide, then emit control for node 4 with decided, accepted and reconfig.

comparisons.description: Control: node 4, which never accepted the StopSign before the sync, must read the reconfiguration as decided after re-decision.
Node 5, which already held the StopSign, should also end at accepted 5; the predicate is expected to be violated with accepted 6.
